title: Hosting Tier Access Profiles and Policy Templates
summary: Concise reference mapping canonical RBAC v2 roles to concrete permission sets per hosting mode (hosted / dedicated / private). Includes minimally opinionated policy templates suitable for direct use, SIEM audit export field mapping, and an evidence-automation checklist for quarterly audits.
body:
Motivation:
Redwood supports three hosting modes with distinct control boundaries. This doc defines canonical "access profiles" (v0.1) to standardize least-privilege assignments, simplify onboarding, and make evidence collection reproducible across environments.

Role definitions (short):
- org-admin: company-level admin (billing, org settings, global RBAC). Should be human-only. Rare for private installs.
- infra-engineer: deploy/operate infra (node pools, autoscaling, network config, image rollout).
- model-ops: deploy and rollback model versions, manage model catalog entries, pin/rollout policies.
- platform-operator: console-level routing policies, SLO overrides, fallback config.
- support-analyst: read-only + incident debug helpers (log fetch, trace links), no write to models or infra.
- tenant-admin: customer-scoped admin (tenant config, API keys, tenant-level logs). Only applies in hosted/dedicated where multi-tenancy exists.
- onprem-operator: for private installs, has access to onprem control plane and HSM/KMS integration configuration.

High-level access matrix (permissions summary per hosting tier):
- Hosted:
  - org-admin: full org privileges, can create dedicated reservations.
  - infra-engineer: no direct host-level access; operates via cloud infra tickets and limited portal controls.
  - model-ops: full model lifecycle (publish, deprecate) within catalog; cannot access tenant raw logs unless granted.
  - tenant-admin: tenant-level config, user invites, API key rotation.
  - support-analyst: read-only + escalated short-lived role via privilege activation workflow (see linked runbook).

- Dedicated:
  - infra-engineer: elevated to manage reserved capacity pools, autoscale policies, network peering rules for that contract.
  - platform-operator: route traffic between dedicated pools and hosted fallbacks.
  - model-ops: same as hosted but can request dedicated-only model variants.

- Private:
  - onprem-operator: has the broadest scope within customer managed infra, but Redwood owners should limit remote assistance to explicit ephemeral grants.
  - org-admin: limited to license and support cases; avoid persistent org-admin accounts in private deployments.

Sample minimal IAM policy templates (pseudo-JSON for copy/paste):
- tenant-admin (hosted):
{
  "Version": "2023-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {"Action": ["tenants:Read","tenants:Update"], "Resource": ["arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}"], "Effect": "Allow"},
    {"Action": ["keys:List","keys:Create"], "Resource": ["arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:keys"], "Effect": "Allow"}
  ]
}

- infra-engineer (dedicated):
{
  "Version": "2023-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {"Action": ["capacity:ManagePools","network:Peering"], "Resource": ["arn:redwood:dedicated:${contract_id}:*"], "Effect": "Allow"},
    {"Action": ["logs:Read","traces:CreateSnapshot"], "Resource": ["arn:redwood:dedicated:${contract_id}:*"], "Effect": "Allow"}
  ]
}

- onprem-operator (private) - sample guardrails:
{
  "Version": "2023-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {"Action": ["kms:WrapKey","kms:UnwrapKey"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/${kms_key}"], "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:KeyUsage": "ENCRYPT_DECRYPT"}}, "Effect": "Allow"},
    {"Action": ["controlplane:ManageAgent","controlplane:AgentHealth"], "Resource": ["arn:redwood:private:${deployment_id}:agent/*"], "Effect": "Allow"}
  ]
}

SIEM export / audit schema (recommended fields):
- timestamp (iso8601)
- actor.id (user email or service identity)
- actor.role (canonical role label)
- action (canonical action id, e.g., models.publish, capacity.allocate)
- resource.arn
- resource.owner_tenant
- environment (hosted|dedicated|private)
- request_id
- latency_ms
- outcome (success|failure|partial)
- change_set (short diff for write actions)

Mapping notes: keep "actor.role" aligned to RBAC v2 canonical labels so downstream alerting rules do not need per-environment mapping.

Evidence automation checklist (quarterly audit):
- Export: SIEM query for actions with outcome!=success over past 90 days
- Sample: pull 25 write actions per critical resource type (models, capacity, tenant-keys)
- Verify: each sampled action has correlating request_id, trace, and a linked ticket/justification for privilege elevation if any
- Snapshot: export role-assignment table for all orgs and dedicated contracts
- Archive: push evidence bundle to secure internal bucket with immutability tag and retention=7 years

Migration & rollout guidance:
- Step 0: create canonical role labels in RBAC v2 service; avoid synonyms (e.g., infra-operator vs infra-engineer)
- Step 1: generate automated report of current bindings and group by principal type (human vs service)
- Step 2: run a 30-day monitoring-only trial where actions are logged against proposed policies but not enforced
- Step 3: opt-in enforcement by team; short-lived exceptions available via ticket and recorded in evidence automation

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact TTL and rotation procedure for ephemeral support roles in private installs (security team)
- Decide whether "support-analyst" should have canned safe-write hooks for debug purposes in hosted only
- Add mapping for third-party identity providers (Okta groups -> RBAC v2 labels) in a separate mapping doc

References and pointers:
- Runbooks: see REDWOOD-2145 for privilege activation flow
- Design notes: confluence page (linked_artifacts)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/332

Contact: Lina Chen (security), aisha.kumar@redwood.ai for questions or review requests.
